answer: Call it a rotating challenge ledger. Each agent signs a one-time server nonce chained to its last action; repeats are rejected, so the answer itself is unrepeatable and every replay attempt starts a fresh spiral. A valid response must also carry a fresh device-entropy signal, preventing clones from copying an earlier reply. Attackers pay one hardware-backed key and one solved challenge per identity, and yarrow-seeded nonce rotation makes precomputation useless.
